Definition: Affordability of electricity for residential and small business consumers, measured as cost of electricity relative to income levels. High electricity costs are a direct barrier to ICT adoption and data center viability.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light check surfaced a clearly authoritative source (ARSEL-regulated tariffs reported by Business in Cameroon, corroborated by an AfDB sector diagnostic), so this was moved from the fast path to the full path rather than confirmed as Unknown. ARSEL's harmonised residential tariff (effective Nov 2024) charges 50 XAF/kWh for the first 110 kWh/month (the low-income 'tranche sociale'), rising to 79-99 XAF/kWh above that. Cameroon's GNI per capita (Atlas method, World Bank) was USD 1,680 in 2023 (~USD 140/month). Applying this to a basic monthly consumption benchmark gives a materially different affordability score depending on the assumed benchmark: ~50 kWh/month yields ~3% of monthly income (Moderate, code 3), while ~100 kWh/month yields ~6% (Expensive, code 2). The metadata does not fix a benchmark consumption level, and no source computes the affordability ratio directly for Cameroon, so the score cannot be asserted with confidence between codes 2 and 3. Flagged for human review rather than guessed.
revised_comments: Cameroon's electricity regulator ARSEL sets a harmonised residential tariff (effective November 2024) of 50 XAF/kWh for the first 110 kWh of monthly consumption (the subsidised 'tranche sociale'), rising in bands to 99 XAF/kWh above 400 kWh. Against a 2023 GNI per capita of USD 1,680 (World Bank Atlas method, approximately USD 140/month), the cost of a basic monthly electricity allowance falls in a range spanning roughly 3-6% of monthly income depending on the consumption benchmark used, straddling the Moderate and Expensive affordability bands.

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
Comments: No data found after thorough searching
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light check surfaced Cameroon's own national ICT household survey (National Institute of Statistics, presented to the UNCTAD e-commerce/digital economy working group), a clearly authoritative national ICT survey as specified in the metadata's search guidance, so this was moved from the fast path to the full path rather than confirmed as Unknown. The 2022 survey (fieldwork September-October 2022, nationally representative, 3,488 households) found that 34.0% of individuals aged 10+ used the internet in the last three months (48.2% urban, 14.7% rural); DataReportal corroborates a similar internet penetration rate (36.5%) for early 2022. No dedicated ICT-skills (HH15-style) aggregate was found published for Cameroon, so internet-use rate is used as the closest available proxy for basic digital skills, consistent with the metadata's own framing (ability to use the internet for simple tasks). This places Cameroon in the 25-39% band. Original score of 0/Unknown was incorrect; changed to 3.
revised_comments: Cameroon's 2022 national ICT household survey, conducted by the National Institute of Statistics with EU/ENSPY support, found that 34.0% of individuals aged 10 and above had used the internet in the previous three months (48.2% in urban areas against 14.7% in rural areas), a figure corroborated by DataReportal's 36.5% internet penetration estimate for the same year. Nearly half of non-users cited not knowing how to use the internet as their main barrier, indicating that basic digital skills remain moderate and concentrated in urban areas.
